findings.issue: contradicts task clause "keep behaviour identical": _phase_entry used `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` and now uses head_sha, whose _ask_head runs plain `git rev-parse HEAD`. On an unborn branch with a root entry named HEAD, git exits 0 and prints the literal string "HEAD". On macOS's case-insensitive filesystem a `head` or `Head` file or directory has the same effect. `--verify -q` exits 1 in that case. head_sha returns "HEAD" even though its docstring says it returns 'the commit HEAD names, or None'. `start` then skips the 'has no commit yet ... commit first' refusal and returns state cut with baseRef "HEAD". The memo cannot catch this: _files_head returns None for an unborn branch, so the answer comes straight from git. Reproduced in scratchpad/p14310/rev/headfile2.sh (unborn plus `head` file: plain exit 0 'HEAD'; plus `Head` directory: exit 0 'HEAD'; with nothing there: exit 128) and in rev/probe_head.py case 11 (head_sha='HEAD', --verify=None). The existing case pe6 (tests/test_audit_task.py:9682) builds an unborn repo with no such entry, so it stays green.
findings.resolution: Have _ask_head ask `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, and have head_sha return None unless the answer matches _OBJECT_NAME. That also makes drive-phase.git_head stricter in the same edge, where it is already pre-existing. Add an sc-hd case with an unborn repo holding a `head` directory, asserting None, and confirm it is red against the plain spelling.

findings.issue: _ref_file returns b"" both for a missing file and for an existing zero-length file, so a zero-length loose ref counts as 'no loose file' and packed-refs answers. Git refuses that ref as broken; this is the empty-ref-after-power-loss state. Once a process has memoised the packed answer, head_sha keeps returning that commit while git returns nothing. Probe case 3 in rev/probe_head.py: head_sha='4e7928d2...', git=None. Git never writes this state itself (it uses lock-and-rename), so it needs a corrupt repository.
findings.resolution: Tell missing apart from empty. Have _ref_file return b"" only on FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError and None for an existing empty file, so _files_head returns None and git is asked.

findings.issue: The _tracking docstring claims 'the same answer one listing each would give', and two shapes break it. (a) A trailing-slash spec naming a gitlink: `sm/` against a submodule `sm` is tracked when asked alone and untracked when batched, because _spec_holds requires `path.startswith('sm/')` and git lists `sm`. (b) GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 in the environment: `Docs`, `DOCS/x.txt` and `.Claude/a.json` are tracked when asked alone and untracked when batched. Both come from rev/probe_head.py section 13. The one caller, plugin_owned_rels, asks only CONFIG_NAME and GITIGNORE_NAME as fixed lower-case file paths, so neither shape is reachable today. The claim is still wider than the code.
findings.resolution: Have _plain_pathspec refuse a spec ending in '/' and refuse batching whenever GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS is set, so those are asked alone. Alternatively, narrow the docstring to the shapes the matcher reproduces.

preExisting.issue: Before this diff, git_head already used plain `rev-parse HEAD` and could return the string "HEAD" in the unborn-plus-HEAD-entry case described in finding 1.
preExisting.resolution: This is covered by finding 1's fix in _ask_head.

intent.note: CLAUSE "Cut those calls in the product ... drive-phase.py carry_git/git_head, _scoped_commit, _tree_stamp, _worktrees._git, audit-task._git_answer, and per-verb git config reads (usage_ledger.resolve_author, _panel_viewer._git_config_origins)". The diff cuts git_head (`+ return _scoped_commit.head_sha(ctx["gitRoot"])`), _scoped_commit._tracking (one `ls-files -z --` listing), _tree_stamp._content_reading (one `ls-files -z -t -s --cached --modified --deleted --others --exclude-standard`) and two of audit-task's _git_answer sites. carry_git, _worktrees._git, usage_ledger.resolve_author and _panel_viewer._git_config_origins are untouched; _worktrees.py, usage_ledger.py and _panel_viewer.py have no diff even though they are declared. That is a scope divergence. The executor states it in its NOT CUT list: the test files those cuts need are not declared, and carry_git is covered only through _index_flags/_seed_from_index. CLAUSE "keep behaviour identical": this does not hold in one edge (finding 1): _phase_entry goes from `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` to `head_sha`, which can return the literal 'HEAD'. CLAUSES "re-measure the full sweep quiet twice 20+ minutes apart with the spread, and state the result against 240 s" and "Never re-record .github/sweep-costs.json from darwin" are met. q1 ran 17:37:41Z-17:43:08Z and q2 18:07:34Z-18:13:02Z (the logs and .meta exist), with a 0.48 s spread. The result is stated as 'NOT MET'. `git status` shows .github/ untouched. CLAIM vs DIFF: the outcome describes the diff accurately except two sentences. 'replaces rev-parse --verify -q HEAD, with the same refusal on an unborn branch' is false in finding 1's case. _tracking's 'same answer one listing each would give' is false for gitlink-with-slash and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS (finding 3, unreachable today). The stamp is graded `current` by stamp-verification.py compare (exit 0). CORRECTNESS OF THE HEAD MEMO, as the orchestrator asked: rev/probe_head.py compared head_sha with fresh git across these shapes, and all agreed except a corrupt empty loose ref (finding 2): 25 same-second commits from subprocesses; update-ref back to an older, same-size SHA; GIT_DIR naming another repo after a warm memo; GIT_DIR naming the same repo; core.worktree; HEAD -> refs/heads/Feature with packed Feature and loose feature on a case-insensitive FS; HEAD symbolic to refs/remotes; a symlinked HEAD; a relative-path linked worktree, detached; `git refs migrate` to reftable mid-process; asks from a subdirectory before and after a commit. The memo only ever returns what the ref files say now, and only after git agreed for the same (root, git_dir, common) key. The bytes are compared, not stat'ed, so same-second and same-size moves are seen. _tree_stamp: in ls-files' single per-entry loop, the -t -s lines carry the same `<mode> <sha> <stage>\t<path>` text after the tag. Downstream sorts `tracked` and does sorted(set()) on `differing`, so order and the R+C duplicates cannot move the digest, and stamps recorded before this change still verify. The re-run of the executor's probe (rev/mutations-rerun.out, 18:21:54Z-18:24:05Z) gave 14/14 rows red with a green baseline (77/77, 62/62, 7/7); C2/C4 also turn the inherited tsc2/tsl3/tsd1/tsn1 red. GAIN vs RISK: the measured gain is small. Wall time went from 332.57 s to 326.93/327.41 s, -1.6%; the baseline was sampled once, at a 15-min load near 6. Slot-seconds went from 2561 to 2511/2519 (-1.8%). Product git spawns in the 10 drive-related suites fell 7.3%. The suite saving comes mostly from in-process repeats inside tests. In a short-lived production verb, the first head_sha costs up to two git_place spawns plus the ask, unless lock_dir or checkout_top has already asked those keys, so the per-invocation saving is near zero. Leaving the two lows aside, the residual risk of the memo itself is low. Finding 1 is a real regression and needs fixing before this lands. On these numbers the change earns its place only as a step toward the 240 s target, which needs about 24% more cut. It does not justify itself on its own measured gain.
